Hi Alex,

Thanks for the context and the attachments — those usage sheets are helpful. We have two common approaches that match what you described:

1) Add-on slab (isolated billing): we create a separate add-on slab that bills at a usage-based per-token rate with its own commit/thresholds. This keeps your core product commit untouched and gives the new team visibility and quota isolation.

2) Incremental commit (pooled): you increase your existing committed volume and the incremental tokens are pooled across teams. This typically yields larger blended discounts as commitment grows, but it requires cross-team agreement on allocation and SLAs.

Quick guardrail suggestions for bursts: set a soft burst cap with automatic throttling + notify-before-overflow alerts (we can cap by route/model). For the short-term commits: we credit incremental quarterly commits pro-rata against an annual commit if you roll them into an annual agreement within 90 days.

Im looping in Lauren (pricing) and Monica (CS/ops) to propose concrete banding and a short proposal. Thu morning PT works for me; what time do you prefer?

Thanks,

Hi all,

Thanks for the details — putting some concrete numbers on the table so we can move fast. These are starting points; well lock final numbers in a formal proposal.

Proposal A: Add-on slab (isolated)
- 0-3M tokens / month: list price (no discount)
- 3-12M tokens / month: 6% off list
- 12-40M tokens / month: 13% off list
- >40M tokens / month: 20% off list
Notes: Monthly settlement, separate invoice, isolated quotas. Ideal if you want strong tenancy boundaries.

Proposal B: Incremental pooled commit (recommended if you intend to consolidate)
- If you add an incremental committed volume to your corporate commit: blended uplift scales at these breakpoints for the incremental slab only: 5% at +5M, 11% at +20M, 16% at +60M (applies to incremental portion).
- Ramp credits: if you commit quarterly for the remainder of the year and convert to an annual within 90 days, we apply a 50% pro-rata credit towards the annual commit.

Operational controls we recommend:
- Route-based burst caps (set by model/endpoint)
- Alarm thresholds at 70%/90% of slab to avoid surprises
- Optional per-route sampling to verify quality after quantization changes

If youd like a hybrid, we can do a small add-on slab for immediate isolation and plan a phased consolidation into the pooled commit at quarter boundaries.

Ill also prepare a short one-pager comparing total cost at 8M steady vs. 25M burst for each option.

Cheers,
